title: Final Comprehensive Mock Exam (004 Blueprint)
description: Realistic full-length exam simulation matching HashiCorp Terraform Associate 004 domain weighting, tricky questions, and scenarios.

questions.domain: Domain 1: Understand Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Concepts
questions.question: Which of the following is a primary characteristic of immutable infrastructure?
options: A. Servers are SSH'd into and updated in place repeatedly over several years.
B. Infrastructure components are never modified in place; updates are achieved by provisioning entirely new components and terminating the old ones.
C. State files cannot be deleted.
D. Infrastructure that does not require networking.
questions.explanation: Immutable infrastructure treats servers as disposable. Instead of patching or modifying running servers (mutable), new machine images or containers are deployed and old instances terminated.

questions.domain: Domain 2: Understand the Purpose of Terraform
questions.question: How does Terraform differ from configuration management tools like Ansible, Puppet, or Chef?
options: A. Terraform focuses primarily on provisioning the underlying infrastructure components (cloud VMs, networks, storage), whereas configuration management tools focus on configuring software inside running operating systems.
B. Terraform cannot run on Linux.
C. Ansible cannot create AWS resources.
D. Configuration management tools do not use code.
questions.explanation: Terraform is fundamentally an infrastructure orchestrator (provisioning cloud services, networking, IAM). Configuration management tools specialize in configuring packages, files, and daemons on already-provisioned servers.

questions.domain: Domain 3: Understand Terraform Basics
questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'required_version' setting in the 'terraform' block?
options: A. Enforces that only compatible versions of the Terraform CLI binary can execute the configuration, preventing unexpected behavior from unsupported versions.
B. Sets the Linux kernel version.
C. Sets the AWS provider version.
questions.explanation: 'required_version' (e.g. '>= 1.5.0, < 2.0.0') pins the allowed Terraform CLI binary versions, preventing team members with older or newer incompatible CLI versions from running.

questions.domain: Domain 3: Understand Terraform Basics
questions.question: Where does Terraform check for provider plugins if an offline network mirror is configured?
options: A. It always queries registry.terraform.io regardless of config.
B. In the directory or network URL specified in the CLI config 'provider_installation' block.
questions.explanation: In air-gapped or enterprise networks, the CLI configuration's 'provider_installation' block can redirect provider discovery to a filesystem mirror or internal network mirror.

questions.domain: Domain 4: Use Terraform Outside the Core Workflow
questions.question: You execute 'terraform taint aws_instance.api'. What does Terraform do?
options: B. Marks the resource in the state file as degraded/tainted, instructing the next 'terraform apply' to destroy and recreate it.
questions.explanation: 'terraform taint' marks an existing resource in state as tainted. During the next plan/apply, Terraform plans to replace it. In modern Terraform, 'terraform apply -replace=...' is preferred.

questions.domain: Domain 4: Use Terraform Outside the Core Workflow
questions.question: What command undoes the effect of 'terraform taint' before an apply is executed?
questions.explanation: 'terraform untaint <ADDRESS>' clears the tainted status from a resource in state, restoring it to healthy status so it will not be replaced on the next apply.

questions.domain: Domain 5: Interact with Terraform Modules
questions.question: You want to pass a list of subnets into a child module. In the child module's 'variables.tf', how should the variable be declared?
questions.explanation: Module inputs are declared using standard 'variable' blocks. Declaring 'type = list(string)' enforces that callers must supply a list of strings.

questions.domain: Domain 5: Interact with Terraform Modules
questions.question: Can a child module define its own 'backend' block?
options: A. Yes, each child module can write to its own backend.
B. No, only the root module may define a backend block. Child modules must never declare backends.
C. Yes, if it is a local backend.
D. Only if sourced from Git.
questions.explanation: Backend blocks are strictly reserved for the root module. Child modules are purely containers for resources and must never specify a backend.

questions.domain: Domain 6: Use the Core Terraform Workflow
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the 'refresh' phase in 'terraform plan'?
options: A. To download the newest Terraform CLI version.
B. To query provider APIs and update the in-memory state with real-world infrastructure attributes before computing diffs.
C. To reboot all running cloud instances.
D. To clear out expired cache entries.
questions.explanation: During the refresh phase, Terraform queries the cloud APIs for every managed resource to synchronize its in-memory view of reality before diffing against HCL configuration.

questions.domain: Domain 6: Use the Core Terraform Workflow
questions.question: What happens if you run 'terraform apply' and type anything other than 'yes' at the confirmation prompt?
options: B. Terraform cancels the apply immediately and leaves existing infrastructure and state untouched.
C. Terraform applies the changes anyway.
questions.explanation: Terraform strictly requires the literal string 'yes' (case-sensitive) to proceed. Entering anything else (e.g. 'y', 'Y', 'YES', or 'no') safely aborts the apply.

questions.domain: Domain 7: Implement and Maintain State
questions.question: What does 'terraform state pull' output?
options: B. The raw state content directly from the remote backend in JSON format to stdout.
questions.explanation: 'terraform state pull' retrieves the state from the active backend and streams the raw JSON structure to standard output.

questions.domain: Domain 7: Implement and Maintain State
questions.question: You need to rename an entire module in state: from 'module.old_vpc' to 'module.new_vpc'. Which command achieves this?
options: A. terraform state mv module.old_vpc module.new_vpc
B. terraform state rename module.old_vpc module.new_vpc
C. terraform module move old_vpc new_vpc
questions.explanation: 'terraform state mv' works on both individual resources and entire modules. Moving 'module.old_vpc' to 'module.new_vpc' re-keys all nested resources in one command.

questions.domain: Domain 8: Read, Generate, and Modify Configuration
questions.question: What does the 'trimspace("  hello world  \n")' function return?
questions.explanation: 'trimspace()' strips all leading and trailing whitespace characters (spaces, tabs, newlines) from a string, returning 'hello world'.

questions.domain: Domain 8: Read, Generate, and Modify Configuration
questions.question: What will 'element(["a", "b", "c"], 4)' return in Terraform?
options: A. Error: Index out of bounds
B. "b" (it wraps around using modulo arithmetic)
questions.explanation: Unlike standard bracket indexing 'list[index]' (which errors if the index is out of bounds), the 'element(list, index)' function wraps around using modulo arithmetic: index 4 in a 3-element list evaluates to 4 % 3 = index 1 ("b").

questions.domain: Domain 8: Read, Generate, and Modify Configuration
questions.question: Given: locals { tags = { Env = "prod", Owner = "DevOps" } }. How do you access the value of 'Owner'?
questions.explanation: Local values are referenced using the singular prefix 'local.' (not 'locals.'). Map keys can be accessed with dot notation ('local.tags.Owner') or square brackets ('local.tags["Owner"]').

questions.domain: Domain 8: Read, Generate, and Modify Configuration
questions.question: Which of the following expressions checks whether a variable string is NOT null and NOT empty?
questions.explanation: Standard HCL boolean operators '&&' (AND), '||' (OR), and '!=' (not equal) are used: 'var.name != null && var.name != ""'.

questions.domain: Domain 4: Use Terraform Outside the Core Workflow
questions.question: What is the primary role of 'terraform test' compared to external tools like Terratest?
options: A. 'terraform test' runs directly inside Terraform using pure HCL (.tftest.hcl), requiring no Go compiler, no external testing frameworks, and supporting fast mock planning.
C. 'terraform test' only works on Windows.
questions.explanation: Native 'terraform test' allows authoring unit and integration tests directly in HCL without needing Go programming knowledge, third-party libraries, or complex test harnesses.

questions.domain: Domain 8: Read, Generate, and Modify Configuration
questions.question: You want to refactor resource 'aws_instance.server[0]' to 'aws_instance.server["web"]'. What 'moved' block is required?
options: A. moved { from = aws_instance.server[0] to = aws_instance.server["web"] }
B. moved { from = aws_instance.server[0] to = aws_instance.web }
questions.explanation: Moved blocks can transition between count indices and for_each string keys seamlessly: 'moved { from = aws_instance.server[0] to = aws_instance.server["web"] }'.

questions.domain: Domain 8: Read, Generate, and Modify Configuration
questions.question: What does the 'coalesce()' function do?
options: B. Takes any number of arguments and returns the first one that is NOT null and NOT empty string ("").
questions.explanation: 'coalesce(val1, val2, ...)' inspects arguments from left to right and returns the first argument that is non-null and non-empty, commonly used for fallback defaults.

questions.domain: Domain 7: Implement and Maintain State
questions.question: When is it appropriate to delete a state lock manually using 'terraform force-unlock'?
options: A. Every time before running 'terraform apply'.
B. ONLY after you have verified with 100% certainty that the process that acquired the lock is dead and no other engineer or pipeline is actively applying changes.
C. Whenever an apply takes more than 1 minute.
D. When you want to speed up deployments.
questions.explanation: Force-unlocking an active running apply will allow concurrent writes, corrupting the state file. It must only ever be used after confirming that the previous process was abruptly killed.

questions.domain: Domain 9: Understand Terraform Cloud/Enterprise Capabilities
questions.question: What happens if a 'Hard Mandatory' Sentinel policy fails in Terraform Cloud?
options: A. The plan can be overridden by a team lead.
B. The run is immediately stopped and CANNOT be applied under any circumstances; the violation must be fixed in code.
C. The changes are applied with a warning.
D. The user's account is locked.
questions.explanation: Hard Mandatory is the strictest enforcement tier. Unlike Soft Mandatory, no user (not even an organization owner) can override a Hard Mandatory failure.

questions.domain: Domain 8: Read, Generate, and Modify Configuration
questions.question: What is the return value of 'jsondecode("{\"port\": 8080}")'?
options: B. A native HCL object/map: { port = 8080 }
questions.explanation: 'jsondecode()' takes a valid JSON string and parses it into corresponding HCL maps, objects, numbers, and lists.

questions.domain: Domain 6: Use the Core Terraform Workflow
questions.question: What is the effect of running 'terraform init -reconfigure'?
options: B. Disregards any existing backend configuration and reinitializes backend from scratch, ignoring previous state migration questions.
questions.explanation: '-reconfigure' forces Terraform to reconfigure the backend from scratch, ignoring any existing state file or prior settings, without offering to migrate existing state.

questions.domain: Domain 8: Read, Generate, and Modify Configuration
questions.question: What does 'distinct(["a", "b", "a", "c"])' return?
questions.explanation: 'distinct(list)' returns a new list with any duplicate elements removed, preserving the relative order of first appearance.

questions.domain: Domain 1: Understand Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Concepts
questions.question: What is the core definition of 'Idempotency' in Infrastructure as Code?
options: A. The system runs 10 times faster with each execution.
B. Executing the same configuration multiple times results in the exact same infrastructure state, without unintended side effects or duplicate resource creation.
C. All code is converted into immutable Docker images.
questions.explanation: Idempotency means that executing 'terraform apply' once or a hundred times against an unchanged environment results in the exact same infrastructure state without altering or duplicating resources.
